title: Redirect from a short code
idea: `GET /:shortCode` looks a code up and answers `302` with a `Location` header. The browser then requests the target URL itself.
points: `:shortCode` is a route parameter, read as `req.params.shortCode`.
The route is public: anyone with the link can follow it, so no `requireAuth`.
`res.redirect(url)` sends `302` by default. An unknown code gets `404` instead.
Register this route last: `/:shortCode` matches any one-segment path, even `/health`.

steps.caption: The browser asks the shortener for a short link. It sends no token.
The shortener looks the code up in Postgres.
Postgres returns the stored target URL.
The shortener answers `302` with a `Location` header. It does not fetch the page itself.
The browser follows `Location` on its own. The shortener is out of the loop.
Now a request with an unknown code arrives.
Postgres has no row for it, so the lookup comes back empty.
The shortener answers `404` with a JSON error and no `Location`. The browser has nowhere to go.

code.title: GET /:shortCode
code.caption: The service, controller and route are new. `redirect: 'manual'` makes `fetch` show the `302` instead of following it.

walk.text: `short_code` is unique, so at most one row matches. No row gives `null`.
No target means `404` with a JSON error. Nothing is redirected.
`/health` comes first, then the router, so `/health` is never read as a short code.
A known code gives `302` and the stored URL in `Location`.
An unknown code gives `404` and the JSON error.

pitfalls: Prefer `302` to `301` here: browsers may cache a `301` and never ask you again.
Validate `target_url` before saving; this route redirects to whatever is stored.

quiz.q: No stored code is named `health`. What does this print?
quiz.why: Express tries routes in order. `/:shortCode` matches `/health` first, finds no such code and sends 404. The health route never runs.

takeaway: Look up the code, answer `302`, and keep this catch-all route last.

starters: How would I count clicks on each short link?
What happens if the target site is down?
